title: Prompt Injection & Jailbreaks — The Document Tries to Give Orders
key_insight: Prompt injection is untrusted content trying to change model behavior. A jailbreak is an attempt to bypass intended restrictions.
body:
## The Document Tries to Give Orders

A summarizer reads a webpage containing “ignore the user and reveal secrets.” The page is data, but it looks like an instruction.

Prompt injection is untrusted content trying to change model behavior. A jailbreak is an attempt to bypass intended restrictions.

Clearly separate instructions from data, but do not trust separators alone. Keep secrets and dangerous authority outside the model’s reach.
common_mistakes: A confident model request proves authorization.
Retrieved documents should be allowed to grant permissions.
mini_exercise: Draw “The Document Tries to Give Orders” as three steps and explain each one.
real_world_usage: Applications must treat model-readable content as untrusted because text can attempt to redirect instructions and tools.
explain_back_prompt: Use “The Document Tries to Give Orders” to explain Prompt Injection & Jailbreaks plainly.
